newsitem.title: POLAND: EBRD offers Poland help in banks' privatisation.
newsitem.headline: EBRD offers Poland help in banks' privatisation.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is willing to keep helping Poland privatise banks and other financial institutions, EBRD President Jacques de Larosiere said on Tuesday.

Asked at a news conference whether or not the EBRD would be ready to take part in upcoming privatisations of Bank Handlowy SA and insurer Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen (PZU), de Larosiere said: "Very much so...we have already done (such) deals...and we are always ready to help."
The EBRD helped Poland privatise Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA (WBK) and Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA by taking equity stakes in them.
De Larosiere also did not rule out helping Poland restructure its largest agriculture bank, Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ), but said it was too early to talk about any specifics.

"We have been asked to look into the BGZ situation, we are indeed studying it closely and I can say even though it's early that we stand ready to participate constructively in finding a solution..." he said.

De Larosiere stressed that the EBRD remained committed to Poland, despite some suggestions that, along with some of the other more advanced east European economies, Poland should be graduated from the list of EBRD help recipients.
The EBRD was set to continue its support for reforming economies as long as there were projects, which could not be financed on a fully commercial basis.

De Larosiere said last year that the EBRD injected into Polish projects a record 278 million Ecus ($355 million), bringing the total sum invested in Poland since the bank's launch in 1991 to 1.2 billion Ecu. He said this year's investment might reach up to about $250 million. But this depended on how many suitable projects would be available.
De Larosiere said the measure of EBRD's confidence in Poland was the high share of equity investments in its spending.
"The EBRD has put 40 percent of its business in Poland in equity, which is two times more than the average we do in EBRD usually," he said.
